newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Renel signs $160 mln loan for fuel imports.
newsitem.headline: Romania Renel signs $160 mln loan for fuel imports.

text.p: Romanian electricity authority Renel RA on Tuesday signed a $160 million syndicated loan, the first corporate raising by a Romanian company on the international markets, for fuel imports this winter.
The syndicated trade finance facility loan was arranged by ING Bank. Co-arrangers are Bank of America NT&SA, BHF-Bank Aktiengesellschaft, Societe Generale and Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi.

"This debut for a Romanian corporate was well received by the international financial market since the arranger was able to close the syndicate in a very short time," said Anthony van der Heijden, general manager of ING Bank Bucharest branch.
ING was mandated to arrange the syndication in October.
Renel president Victor Romert said the $160 million loan would be used to finance the import of 1.3 million tonnes of fuel oil in the coming winter months.

The London branch of Banque Francaise du Commerce Exterieur, BBL Ireland and Royal Bank of Canada were lead managers and Bayerische Landesbank Girozentrale and the London branch of GiroCredit Bank acted as managers.
Details of the terms of the loan were not available.

"This transaction will have its benefits for the future borrowings of Romania's corporate sector from the international markets," said Jean Bonnet, manager of ING Bank Amsterdam syndication department.
Last winter, an acute shortage of hard currency forced Romania to reduce fuel imports and the state-run Renel had to cut power supplies to industrial sectors over January-March.
Banking sources told Reuters recently Renel was planning further raisings on the international markets next year, possibly a Eurbond issue through the U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch.

After an absence of more than a decade, Romania re-entered international capital markets last year with syndicated loans for the National Bank of Romania, which also launced the first Samurai and Eurobond issues this year.

Romania won its first credit ratings from major agencies in March. Japan Credit Rating agency awarded it a BB-plus, somewhat higher than the BB- minus ratings of Standard and Poor's and IBCA and BA-three from Moody's Investors Service.
